````text
# #3846: Patch: follow-up to #3809 from the after-merge spot-check
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

<!-- jackioh-bot:spot-check-follow-up #3809 -->
The after-merge spot-check of #3809 ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/43392834109)) found 1 blocking problem(s) in the change as it merged (`d412e3fd9fc3`). `claude-1` (claude, `opus`, strong) reviewed it. #3809 stays merged: nothing is reverted, and this issue fixes what it found in a change of its own, from `main`.

## What to fix

- [ ] `apps/web/src/routes/play.tsx:459`: When the game server itself is down, the notice never appears: the edge Worker answers that request with a 500 or 503, and the catch treats any `ApiRequestError` as proof the server was reached, so it resets the count and clears the notice.
  Evidence: The catch counts only `cause instanceof ApiUnreachableError`; every other rejection runs `failedReads.current = 0; setUnreachable(false)` (play.tsx:459-468). In production `/api/*` goes through the edge Worker, and apps/edge/src/index.ts:118 says `containerFetch` "turns a failed or aborted fetch into a 500 (or 503, 429) answer rather than rejecting". When the server container is crashed, restarting or not answering, `getMe` therefore rejects with `ApiRequestError(500|503)` (api.ts: `if (!response.ok) throw new ApiRequestError(...)`), never with `ApiUnreachableError`. In that state the queue screen still says "In the queue" with no notice, which is the bug #3792 describes; the player finds out only when the server returns and two reads say `queued: false`. R3792000's 'Clearing' and 'Rejected' paragraphs say a 5xx "proves the server was reached". For this deployment that is false: it proves only that the edge answered. The test 'R3792000 a read the server refused is not an unreachable one' uses `ApiRequestError(503, …)`, so it locks this gap in. Fix: count gateway-style answers (status >= 500, or at least 500/502/503/504) as unreachable and keep 4xx (401, 403, 404, 429) as reached. Amend R3792000 with a new ruling in the follow-up issue's block, and change that test to a 4xx while adding one where a run of 503s shows the notice.

## Done when

- Each finding above is fixed where it points, or answered with the evidence that it does not hold.
- Every check is green, with no test skipped, ignored or weakened to get there (CLAUDE.md rule 12).

---
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot from the after-merge spot-check (one in 5 medium or hard merges, `spot_check_every`): `claude-8` (`claude`) built #3809 and `claude-8` (`opus`) approved it. This issue's own pull request is never spot-checked.

<!-- jackioh-bot -->

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by `claude-6` (claude, `sonnet`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/43404565969)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

`/play`'s wait must show the "Can't reach the server. Still trying…" notice when the edge Worker answers a wait's account read with a gateway-style status (500 or above). Today only `ApiUnreachableError` counts, so a crashed or restarting game server (which the Worker reports as a 500 or 503) shows no notice. A 4xx (401, 403, 404, 429) still proves the server was reached and clears the notice. A new ruling, R3846000, amends R3792000. The test that locked the gap in becomes a 4xx test, and a new test shows a run of 503s raising the notice.

## Files to touch

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `apps/web/src/routes/play.tsx` | Add constant `FIRST_UNREACHABLE_STATUS = 500` and a helper `isUnreachableRead(cause)`. Use the helper in `useLobbyWatch`'s `.catch`. Update the `useLobbyWatch` doc comment and the comment on `LOBBY_UNREACHABLE_AFTER_READS`. |
| `apps/web/src/routes/play.test.tsx` | In `describe("R3792000 …")`, change the "refused" test to a 4xx and add the 5xx tests. Add an R3846000 `describe`. |
| `spec/rulings/R3846000.md` | new: the ruling. |
| `spec/pending/3846.md` | new: its §11 paragraph. |
| `spec/rulings/R3792000.md` | Edit the "Clearing", "Rejected" and "The rule" paragraphs to point at [[R3846000]]. |
| `spec/11-rulings.md` | Edit the already-folded R3792000 paragraph (line ~2100) in place, adding the amendment. Touch nothing else in the file. |

Do not touch these: `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, `apps/web/src/net/api.ts`, `apps/edge/`, any crate, `spec/INDEX.md`. Never run `cargo jackioh spec index` or `spec fold`. Governing rulings: R3792000 (amended), R897000, R3205000, CLAUDE.md rules 3, 7 and 9.

## Steps

1. **`apps/web/src/routes/play.tsx`, constants.** Next to `LOBBY_UNREACHABLE_AFTER_READS` (line ~80) add:
   ```ts
   /** R3846000: the first status of an answer that says the server was not reached: in production the edge Worker answers for a server that is down with a 500, 502, 503 or 504 (`apps/edge/src/index.ts`, `containerFetch`). */
   const FIRST_UNREACHABLE_STATUS = 500;
   ```
   Also change the comment on `LOBBY_UNREACHABLE_AFTER_READS` from "(the server unreachable)" to "(the server unreachable, or answering 5xx, R3846000)".

2. **Same file, helper.** Above `useLobbyWatch` (it already imports `ApiUnreachableError`; add `ApiRequestError` to the existing `../net/api.ts` import list, line ~28):
   ```ts
   /** R3846000: a read that did not reach the game server: a transport failure or timeout, or the edge's 5xx answer for a server that is down. A 4xx proves the server was reached. */
   function isUnreachableRead(cause: unknown): boolean {
     return (
       cause instanceof ApiUnreachableError ||
       (cause instanceof ApiRequestError && cause.status >= FIRST_UNREACHABLE_STATUS)
     );
   }
   ```

3. **`useLobbyWatch`'s `.catch`** (line ~466). Replace `if (cause instanceof ApiUnreachableError)` with `if (isUnreachableRead(cause))`. Change the else comment to "The server answered (a refusal: 4xx): reached, so the count starts again." Leave the success path (`.then`) alone, and leave the `ended`/`endedReads` logic alone: a failed read still counts neither way. Update the doc comment above `useLobbyWatch` ("failed unreachable" to "failed unreachable (a transport failure, a timeout or a 5xx answer)").

4. **`apps/web/src/routes/play.test.tsx`.**
   - Change the test at line 1605. Rename it `"R3792000 a read the server refused with a 4xx is not an unreachable one"`. Use `new ApiRequestError(403, { code: "forbidden", message: "No." })` and keep the rest.
   - Add after it, in the same `describe`, `"R3846000 a run of 5xx answers shows the notice like unreachable reads"`. It mocks `getMe` with `mockRejectedValue(new ApiRequestError(503, { code: "unavailable", message: "Try again." }))`, runs `await waitReads(LOBBY_UNREACHABLE_AFTER_READS)`, then asserts the notice (`playTestid.unreachable`) has text `NOTICE`, the queue line (`playTestid.status`) still reads `In the ${MODE_LABEL.bo1} queue.`, and `getMe` was called `LOBBY_UNREACHABLE_AFTER_READS` times.
   - Add `"R3846000 fewer 5xx answers than the constant show nothing"`: 500 for `LOBBY_UNREACHABLE_AFTER_READS - 1` reads, no notice.
   - Add `"R3846000 a 4xx answer after the notice clears it and starts the count again"`. Reach the notice with 503s, then `mockRejectedValue(new ApiRequestError(401, …))`, `await settle({ advance: ACCOUNT_MS })`, and assert the notice is gone. Then mock 503 again, settle `LOBBY_UNREACHABLE_AFTER_READS - 1` times (no notice), and settle once more (notice). Copy the shape of the test at line 1577.
   - Add `"R3846000 a mixed run of transport failures and 5xx answers counts together"`: mock `getMe` with `mockRejectedValueOnce(new ApiUnreachableError(new TypeError("Failed to fetch")))` for the first read, then `.mockRejectedValue(new ApiRequestError(502, …))`. After `waitReads(LOBBY_UNREACHABLE_AFTER_READS)` the notice shows.
   - Since the new tests sit inside `describe("R3792000 …")` and use `waitReads`, `down` and `NOTICE`, add them there. Every title must contain `R3846000` as a word so `spec check` counts it as proof.

5. **`spec/rulings/R3846000.md`** (front matter as in `spec/rulings/R3792000.md`):
   ```
   ---
   id: R3846000
   title: "A wait's reads answered with a 5xx count as unreachable (issue #3846; amends R3792000)"
   cards: "§9.5, R3792000, R897000, issue #3846, issue #3809"
   proven_in:
     - apps/web/src/routes/play.test.tsx
   ---
   ```
   The body is four paragraphs:
   - **Why.** [[R3792000]] counted only `ApiUnreachableError`, but in production `/api/*` goes through the edge Worker, whose `containerFetch` answers 500 (or 503, 502, 504) for a server that is crashed, restarting or silent. Those reads rejected as `ApiRequestError`, reset the count and cleared the notice, so the queue screen said "In the queue" with no notice while the server had dropped the ticket.
   - **The rule.** A read of a wait fails as unreachable when it rejects with `ApiUnreachableError` or with an `ApiRequestError` whose status is at least `FIRST_UNREACHABLE_STATUS` (500, `routes/play.tsx`). Such reads count together toward `LOBBY_UNREACHABLE_AFTER_READS`. A 4xx (401, 403, 404, 429) still proves the server was reached, clears the notice and resets the count. This replaces R3792000's "a refusal, a 5xx" wording.
   - **Unchanged.** The threshold, the notice, the ticket logic ([[R897000]]) and presentation-only (CLAUDE.md rule 7).
   - **Rejected.** Listing 500, 502, 503 and 504 only (a 501 or 507 from the edge would then clear the notice, and the Worker's own 5xx all mean it could not get an answer); counting 429 (the Worker uses it for a throttled container, but the issue keeps it as reached, and a throttle is the server being alive); counting every rejection (a 401 would look like an outage).

6. **`spec/pending/3846.md`**: one paragraph, in the form of the one in `spec/pending/3791.md`: `**[[R3846000]] A wait's reads answered with a 5xx count as unreachable (issue #3846, 2026-11-13)**: amends [[R3792000]]. …` Summarize the rule in 2–3 sentences, and say the Worker answers 5xx for a down server.

7. **`spec/rulings/R3792000.md`.**
   - "The rule": after "(`ApiUnreachableError`: a transport failure or a timeout)" add "or, per [[R3846000]], a 5xx answer".
   - "Clearing": replace "including one that was refused (an `ApiRequestError`, which proves the server was reached and is not counted as a failure)" with "including one that was refused with a 4xx (an `ApiRequestError` below 500, which proves the server was reached; a 5xx counts as a failure, [[R3846000]])".
   - "Rejected": change "a 401 or a 5xx an outage" to "a 401 an outage".

8. **`spec/11-rulings.md` line ~2100.** Edit the R3792000 paragraph in place with the same two changes: "fail as unreachable (`ApiUnreachableError`, or a 5xx answer, [[R3846000]])" and "a refusal among them" becomes "a 4xx refusal among them". Change nothing else in the file.

## Tests

Commands:
- `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/routes/play.test.tsx` (the whole file, so the R3207003 and other lobby tests still pass).
- `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`
- `pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/routes`
- `cargo jackioh spec check`

## Done when

- [ ] A run of 503, 502 or 500 reads shows the notice, and a mixed run with transport failures also shows it.
- [ ] A 4xx read clears the notice and resets the count (the changed test uses 403, a new one 401).
- [ ] R3846000 is added, with its `spec/pending/3846.md` paragraph. R3792000's note and its folded paragraph are amended.
- [ ] `play.test.tsx` passes, with no skip, `.only` or weakening.
- [ ] `spec check`, web typecheck and eslint, `cargo fmt --check`, and the harness's web tests pass.
- [ ] No hard-coded 500 outside the named constant.

## Risks

- `spec check` fails if a test title lacks `R3846000` as a word, or if the note's `cards` names a missing ruling. Use the exact title formats above.
- The 5xx definition is broad. A real server 500 on `/api/auth/me` (a server bug) also raises the notice. That is acceptable: the player still cannot use the wait, and the next good read clears the notice.
- `getMe`'s own 401 path (an expired session) is handled elsewhere. A 401 stays "reached", so there is no behavior change there.
- Fake timers in this `describe` fake only `setInterval` and `clearInterval`. Use the existing `settle` and `waitReads` helpers unchanged.

## Open questions

None.
````
